data.narrative:
Airrow is a seed-stage Defense & Security company founded by Menachem Fehler and David Kaye that has raised $350K to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 10 comparable companies (2 public, 8 private), including same-sector, same/adjacent-stage players such as UFORCE, Stark Defence, Castelion, Singularity, and NODA AI.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-Progression analysis uses the $350K raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $875K. Peer-Median analysis across five Defense & Security comparables (ranging $125M to $4.0B) produces a $1.0B implied valuation. The wide peer range reflects heterogeneity in the sector and staging—Stark Defence and Castelion occupy the $1.0B–$4.0B band, while NODA AI sits at $125M.

The triangulated valuation range is $744K (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $500M. The substantial distance between methods reflects the stage mismatch inherent in using Series A comparables for a seed-stage business. Stage-Progression is most reliable here; the Peer-Median method should be weighted cautiously given that most peers are further advanced. Key uncertainties include customer traction, technical differentiation, and capital efficiency relative to the peer set. Additional near-term data on ARR or pilot customers would narrow this range considerably.
